item.title: The rise of the economic populist: What voters want from both parties this year
item.description: A new kind of economic populism is surging in both parties this year as voters search for a political party that can solve growing concerns about financial stability.
item.content:encoded: A new kind of economic populism is surging in both parties this year as voters search for a political party that can solve growing concerns about financial stability.
item.dc:creator: Mara Liasson

item.title: Week in Politics: Ramaswamy's Ohio ad; Trump greenlights DOJ to sue over Alaska Senate
item.description: Ohio GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy refuses to withdrawal an explosive attack ad, and President Trump greenlights the DOJ to file a lawsuit about Alaska's senate race.
item.content:encoded: Ohio GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy refuses to withdrawal an explosive attack ad, and President Trump greenlights the DOJ to file a lawsuit about Alaska's senate race.

item.title: This decade has been missing its big-impact midterm
item.description: Every other decade over the past hundred years has produced at least one midterm that made a big difference in Congress and in national politics more broadly.

item.title: At a Texas high school football game, fans offer a glimpse into evolving politics
item.description: We talk with voters at a Texas high school football game at the tailgate, in line at the concession booth and in the stands to hear about the issues that matter to Texans this cycle.

item.title: Russia steps up election influence efforts in final stretch of midterms
item.description: Researchers who track online influence operations say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U.S. and around the world.

item.title: The Pentagon's guidelines for "responsible AI" aren't always followed, report shows
item.description: The Pentagon is building weapons and projects with AI capabilities that officials say don't always closely adhere to the agency's own guidelines for AI, according to a congressional watchdog report published in October.

item.title: Ohio could decide control of the Senate. Its rural voters might decide the winner
item.description: Ohio has been a reliably red state for several elections but it's competitive this year. If Democrats want to prevail, they'll have to win people who have backed Republicans, like rural voters.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: A D.C. park was made 'for the pleasure of the people.' Trump's plan would change that
item.description: Trump's most recent rendering of East Potomac Park overtakes the D.C. peninsula with a sprawling golf course, without the grassy areas and road beloved by locals. That's prompted grassroots pushback.

item.title: Military reinforcements move to Mideast. And, millions of Americans vote early
item.description: Military reinforcements are heading to the Middle East and some personnel have left the region, pointing to a potential attack on Iran. And, millions of Americans have already voted in the midterms.
